exclude: DDT repeat-fill between queued SID priorities and the metatile tables. The $0071 write beginning at $9078 has 136 bytes left on that page. $9078 itself is a priority alias and is counted.
DDT repeat-fill $BC between the character staging ring and the expanded map. Confirmed at both boundaries at $0071.
First generated character screen matrix, filled by the title and room drawing routines. The sprite pointer bytes begin at $CBF8.
Second generated character screen matrix. The renderer initializes the first eighteen rows and the remaining cells retain the hand-over fill. The sprite pointer bytes begin at $CFF8.

comments.text: Shared pointer low byte. The room map decoder consumes its packed bytes through the pointer at $02/$03.
High source pointer byte incremented on wrap in the input stream advance helper at $3166.
Low destination pointer byte during room expansion. Routines such as $7671 initially take a grid column here.
High byte of the map destination pointer. The room cell helper initially reads the row here before constructing the full pointer.
Low byte of the auxiliary pointer used by terrain glyph addressing and the bitmap text source calculation.
High auxiliary pointer byte. The title and bitmap paths update it when eight-byte or sixteen-byte glyph indexing crosses a page.
Low byte of the map traversal pointer used by the metatile reuse pass at $431E.
High byte of the map traversal pointer advanced by $3189 when the low byte wraps.
Low byte of the title screen-cell pointer during double-height text and of the glyph target while installing terrain.
High byte of the character output pointer. The terrain glyph installer builds it from the slot index and bank value.
Pixel-source position saved from A at the beginning of the inventory icon copy.
Colour-source position saved from Y during the same copy.
Holds the original letter while title text draws the extra right column for M or W.
Shared text-interpreter scratch in the zero-page workspace.
Shared byte for loop counts, including the character-row transfer and the title menu delay.
Holds the reset copy's record width or a temporarily saved object index, depending on the engine path.
Room setup saves the third charset band's height here. Projectile hit processing also keeps its caller's Y here.
Low byte of the number of cells remaining in the current metatile traversal pass.
High byte of the traversal count checked with the low byte before continuing to another map cell.
High base address of the nominated charset, added when converting an allocated code to an eight-row glyph address.
Movement update sets this selector before the player renderer chooses the relevant sprite pose.
Decrementing counter checked by the movement and rifle paths during their timed handling.
Facing state used by the rifle and bomb templates when choosing their signed horizontal step.
Zero selects keyboard and nonzero selects joystick port two in the input routine.
Low byte of the cell descriptor index derived from the metatile number and in-tile row and column.
High byte of the descriptor index, providing the carry when addressing all sixteen entries of a metatile.
Low byte of the glyph index loaded from the little-endian terrain descriptor.
High byte of the glyph index, also used when forming a pointer to the corresponding colour byte.
Low byte of the cell pointer used to clear or install a thrust effect glyph.
High byte of that pointer. The draw helper derives it from the active screen matrix.
Active-low left latch. The poll stores zero for pressed, with a nonzero bit mask when released.
Active-low right latch. The default keyboard mask is $02 and the joystick mask is $08.
Active-low up latch. Port 2 supplies bit 0 and the default keyboard row supplies bit 6.
Active-low select latch, copied to $28 before each new poll.
Active-low fire latch, copied to $27 before each new poll.
The prior fire sample, retained by the poll before it updates $26.
The prior select sample, retained before $25 is updated.
Index into the raster line and handler selection tables.
Prepared mask or high X state for the player sprite at the raster upload.
Colour of the main player sprite, read by the fixed sprite upload path.
X byte for the player sprite handled outside the sorted object queue.
Y byte written by the player renderer and set to $FF when the room setup hides the sprite.
Counter used by the player draw path to select a phase of the pose.
Current upload list index, advanced through the link array at $297B by the raster handlers.
Increases as objects enter the visible sprite queue. The scene reset helper clears it.
Index into the band-switch arrays when the scheduler combines them with sprite upload events.
Temporary high-X mask used while merging the next sprite into the schedule.
Destination index for the sorted raster entries in the event table.
Main program X preserved by the raster handlers and reloaded before return.
Main program accumulator preserved by the active raster handler.
Main program Y saved while a raster handler uses it to upload sprites.
Preserved index into the visible object list used at the start of sprite scheduling.
Index of the object being scheduled, advanced through the sorted links.
Incremented in the title and engine loops and masked to select periodic display changes.
Current VIC sprite index used for the bit mask tables and advanced as the schedule is written.
Lower bound on the next scheduled scanline, updated after reserving time for a sprite upload or charset switch.
X preserved when entering the lower display's raster routine.
Accumulator saved by the lower bitmap handler until it finishes the mode switch.
Y saved by the lower bitmap handler and restored on its return path.
Low byte of an auxiliary text or terrain destination, including the second glyph row in title text.
High byte of that auxiliary destination, incremented when the second title row crosses a page.
Low byte of the original spawn-list pointer used to save the working list before changing rooms.
High byte of the original spawn-list destination.
Low byte of the source used when moving working interactions back to their room record list.
High byte paired with the original interaction record destination.
Low byte of the room's six-byte persistent state destination.
High byte paired with the destination for the six state bytes.
Low byte of the current room's coordinate and tile override buffer pointer.
High byte for the original interaction record list. The room loader saves it so the transition can write back the mutable copy.
Low byte of the active screen-cell pointer loaded from the twinkle record and read indirectly to check the glyph.
High byte for the same pointer. $0857 loads it from the second byte of the current record before the twinkle check.
Eight screen Y values in the sorted upload order. The IRQ reads this array at $240D when filling the hardware slots.
Eight low screen X bytes. The scheduler clears unused queue entries and fills the rest from the visible object list.
Eight values for the VIC shared register that holds the ninth bit of each sprite's X position.
The sprite graphics pointers in raster upload order. The IRQ copies each to the corresponding slot in both screen matrices.
Scratch register mask accumulated by the sprite scheduler before it saves a copy for each queued update.
Start of the visible Y-coordinate table. The temporary map marker path also uses this byte as the low address of its screen pointer.
Vertical coordinate of the first extra player sprite. The marker routine reuses it as the high byte of its screen pointer.
Further Y coordinates used to order and schedule visible sprites. The player drawing path writes its second extra sprite position here.
Head of the linked list of visible objects sorted for raster uploads, using zero as the end mark.
First reserved link slot. The setup at $2905 points it to object two.
Second reserved link slot, set to zero by $2901. The rest of the page tail holds further visible-object links.
Low byte of the waveform or pitch sequence selected from the runtime effect directory.
High byte of the selected modulation sequence's indirect pointer.
Seven-byte hardware block offset for the current SID voice.
Current voice's four-byte effect-record index while processing modulation.
Working mode flags that select the initial pitch adjustment and supply the filter update bits.
Working modulation parameter, used for early pitch update timing and pitch bend direction.
Working stream offset and timed bend reload value from the effect's third modulation byte.
Three current frequency-low bytes, written to the selected SID voice from $AF01.
First current frequency-high byte, paired with the corresponding low byte for SID writes.
Remaining two frequency-high bytes in the effect driver. The title driver also used this address in its pitch-pattern mode flags.
Holds the cutoff value between the filter initialization and its add-or-subtract update.
Current waveform sequence offset for gameplay voice zero.
Waveform offsets for voices one and two. The earlier title code also indexes a pattern selector from this region.
Saved target offset for the waveform stream's $FF loop command on voice zero.
Saved waveform stream loop positions for the remaining two voices.
Current pitch stream index for the first gameplay voice, reset when a new effect starts.
Corresponding current pitch stream indices for voices one and two.
Saved pitch stream loop anchor for voice zero.
Loop anchors for the remaining two pitch streams. The title driver previously used this region in its live frequency.
First voice's frequency-low base reloaded at the glide timing boundary.
Remaining two low-byte glide bases. Updated together with the high bytes on the pitch-bend paths.
Three high bytes paired with the per-voice frequency-low glide bases.
The game colour table produced by startup at $A08A. Each byte comes from the ninth byte of a terrain glyph's source record with bit 3 set by $A086.
Final 121 entries of the terrain colour plane beginning at $0200. Startup at $A056 writes one colour per source glyph, setting bit 3 in each.
The final 25 per-glyph colour bytes produced by the startup compaction. $46E1 reads this table at $0200 plus the original glyph index.

Screen codes left in the default $0400 screen page after the game's loader passes control to $0600. The packed literals arrange $20 and $A0 blank cells around Commodore border glyphs $69 and $E9. Gameplay selects VIC bank 3 instead.
Jumps to the one-time setup routine at $9FAD. The hand-over snapshot holds that routine before gameplay overwrites its bytes.
Copies seven pages starting at $8921 into VIC RAM at $C000 before setting the title display registers.
Patched source high byte in the title charset copy. It advances after every 256-byte group beginning at $8921.
Patched destination high byte in the title charset copy. It advances after each full group beginning at $C000.
Selects the screen and character bases, enables 25-row text mode, and moves all eight sprite Y coordinates to zero.
Installs the title glyph renderer and IRQ, copies title video data, then alternates title drawing and the keyboard wait.
Prints the title control legend and waits on the raster synchronization path while polling the title input handler. An active handler result returns control to the main title-menu entry at $0656.
Sets VIC shared character colours and copies six 25-character rows from $888B into the title screen, setting their individual colour RAM cells to $0B.

Clears and draws the title logo and menu text. Polls keyboard and assigned controls on raster synchronization, changes the input mode or starts play, and animates the selected input-mode row using the colours at $074E.
Set to $FF after the full keyboard scan equals the stored eight-byte signature.
Sixteen alternating VIC colours, indexed by the low frame-counter nibble at $06F5 and written to the current title menu row.
Eight-byte signature compared byte for byte against the keyboard scan results at $22CC. When all eight bytes agree, the menu sets $074D to $FF.
Display stream passed to $2F70 by $065F. Positions and colours the credits for programming, graphics, music and concept.
Display stream passed to $2F70 by $06C6. Prints the numbered Start Game, Keyboard and Joystick menu choices and the publisher line.
The numbered keyboard and joystick entries and the Probe Software credit finish the title menu stream above this address boundary.
Nested stream from the three menu lines. Repeats the space character six times and returns at $FF.
Clears the paired effect counters and waits for the next signal from the raster handler.
Set when entering play, cleared on the title path and tested by the NMI handler.

Allocates new twinkle positions at $0897, then walks the three-byte records at $9A00. For each live countdown, updates its pointed screen cell only when blank or still holding the twinkle's current glyph.
Nineteen screen codes indexed by each twinkle's countdown. $0845 uses the current entry to check ownership of the screen cell and writes the next one as the counter falls.
Calls the allocator at $089A and falls through to attempt a second allocation in the same update.
Searches backward for an empty countdown in the three-byte records. Chooses random row and column offsets, saves a screen-cell pointer and initializes the glyph countdown to $12.
Zeros byte two of each three-byte slot from $9A00 through the slot at $9A78.
Resets the title state and clears the object slot flags before calling the title loop.
Copies seven pages into $B300 by incrementing the source and destination high operands. The cell snapshot holds the patched operands $EF00 and $B300.
Patched high byte of the SID driver's source operand. The seven-page copy increments it once per page.
Patched high destination operand of the copy into $AC00. The copy advances both operand highs until X counts down from seven.
Changes the audio dispatch flag, prepares the game display and interrupts, and initializes the first gameplay state.
Polls controls before running object and camera updates. The wait at $0987 is bypassed when $0D38 is $02 or $04. The loop returns here at $09CD.
If $09DE is zero, loads it with eight and calls the gauge decrement routine at $6A84.
Pending damage delay aged down before another gauge decrement can be requested.
Decrements $09DE when nonzero, leaving zero unchanged for the next damage check.
Set during visible display preparation. The timed screen effect uses it to skip object handling during that phase.
Set by interaction activation and checked before the equipment selection routine can process another input edge.
Temporary delay shared by the terminal and equipment panel redraw paths.
Byte offset in the 17-byte configuration directory. The room loader reads all of its pointers relative to this byte.
Saves the old room directory offset before running the room change sequence, which can restore it.
Number of active impact slots. The effect allocator checks it before adding another, and the last animation frame decrements it.
Clears initial state at $001A, $1AE1 and $09ED, initializes the arrays at $7C37 and $7C48 from presets, then calls $7C80.
Copies a fixed number of bytes per record from the pointers in $02 and $04. Stops when the last byte of a just-copied record is $FF.
Saved directory index restored on return from the terminator-delimited copy.
Ten five-byte descriptors for resetting mutable room and equipment data. The first byte is the low byte of the destination.
High destination byte of each reset descriptor.
Low source byte of each reset descriptor.
High source byte of each reset descriptor.
The size in bytes for each source record. $0A77 repeats that-sized transfer until it encounters $FF in the last byte.
Tests the player's position against horizontal and vertical thresholds and tests available map margins before setting the scroll request.
Signed horizontal adjustment used when displaying or moving the current transition object.
Signed vertical adjustment paired with the horizontal transition motion byte.
Selects the callback at $0B40/$0B41 for the current camera advance.
Low byte of the direction-indexed camera movement callback.
High byte paired with the low address at $0B40. The scroll update patches its movement call from the direction selected by $0B3F.
Decrements the logical column and the fine X scroll counter. Wraps that counter to fifteen and decrements the coarse column on underflow.
Changing horizontal camera counter used by the scroll update and the map marker.
Changing vertical camera counter, also used to pick the marker's position inside a screen glyph.

Increments the horizontal fine-scroll counter and logical column. On the fine counter reaching 16, increments the coarse column and resets the counter. Uses phase $0D38 to select the new VIC scroll value.
Decrements the logical Y coordinate and wraps the fine-scroll counter to fifteen at a coarse row crossing. Selects a VIC vertical scroll value using the current phase.
Applies the upward movement helper, then the leftward one before returning.
Applies the upward movement helper followed by the rightward helper.
Increments the logical Y coordinate. On a fine-scroll counter reaching sixteen, resets it and increments the coarse row. Selects the VIC vertical scroll value for the current phase.
Applies the downward movement helper and tail-calls the leftward helper.
Applies the downward movement helper and tail-calls the rightward helper.
High byte of the jump target $0B7F, also the first byte that can be read when indexing the adjacent phase data from $0C03.
Remainder of the leftward phase table that begins in the high operand byte of the jump at $0C01.
Four phase choices for horizontal motion toward the right.
Four VIC vertical scroll values for travel downward, indexed by $0D38.
Four phase-dependent VIC vertical scroll values for travel upward.

Inverts the fine scroll nibbles, forms signed 16-bit camera offsets from coarse and fine scroll, and adds Dan's screen position to store world coordinates. Horizontal coordinates remain in half-pixels here and the last two shifts produce the doubled vertical values.
Low byte of Dan's room position in horizontal half-pixels. Computed at $0C8B.
High byte of the room X coordinate after adding the camera offset and carry.
Low byte of the doubled room Y position calculated from Dan's screen Y and the camera at $0C96.
High byte of the doubled room Y coordinate. The final rotate includes carry from doubling its low byte.
The camera schedule copies its countdown here before decrementing it. The dispatcher reads this snapshot of the phase.
Clears the dispatch phase, then advances a pending scroll. At the countdown transition to one it toggles the active screen bit and schedules sprite compensation.
Low byte of the camera movement call patched from the direction table at $0B40.
High operand byte of the $0CDB call to the coordinate-update helper. The next instruction at $0CDF records the scroll phase before advancing it.
Saves the current phase and decrements it. At phase one, flips the selected screen bank, records the movement state and marks the corresponding scroll refresh flags.
Raised when the display bank flips. The sprite adjustment routine clears it after applying the matching motion deltas.
Direction captured at the bank flip and used to index the pair of sprite adjustment bytes at $2473.
Request byte for the marker update. Cleared when the marker display path redraws the position glyph.
Dispatches on values 1–4 from $0CB6 to distinct camera handlers. Zero and other values return immediately.
The main code writes zero to wait. The title raster IRQ decrements it, and the panel IRQ decrements it when zero.
Phase that controls when the active display matrix flips and which VIC fine scroll values are selected.
Coarse Y from $0D3F multiplied by four during room initialization.
Coarse X from $0D41 multiplied by four during room initialization.
Saved logical row restored at the start of the next scroll step.
Saved logical column restored before the camera movement callback is called.
Running source row index while copying staged characters or colours into the hardware screens.
Coarse vertical origin used to calculate the first visible map row.
Camera row position within a 16-step coarse interval.
Coarse horizontal origin used to index the visible map columns.
Camera column position within a 16-step coarse interval.
Inverted fine X coordinate used by the room screen position conversions.
Inverted fine Y coordinate used by the matching vertical conversion.
A room configuration byte compared with camera tile X plus ten before a right scroll is allowed.
A room configuration byte compared with camera tile Y plus five before a down scroll is allowed.
Bit four selects between the two character matrices. The bank switch and draw paths use it when resolving the screen address.
High nibble of the playfield screen/character register value, kept for the intermediate charset switches.
Vertical pixel adjustment added to the player's screen Y in the sprite pose renderer.
Its low three bits feed $D011 in the playfield IRQ. The full value is copied to $0D4C.
Its low three bits feed $D016 in the playfield IRQ.
Copy of the vertical scroll value installed by the main playfield handler and tested by the lower display split.
Takes the vertical direction from bits $08 and $10 of $0B3F and starts from the tile row above or five rows below the camera origin.
Patched high source byte for the indexed fetch of a staged character row. The scroll phase determines which page in the four-by-four metatile plane it reads.
Patched high source byte in the colour load. It selects a page four higher than the character source.
Countdown of the rows still to patch in the active horizontal transfer.
Stored phase byte for the adjacent horizontal staging transfer.

Adds the incoming column delta to the coarse camera X and reads a vertical strip of room tiles from $A600. For the current fine-scroll phase it scatters character codes and colours to matching offsets in the $9A00 and $B400 staging buffers.

Waits for the safe raster region, then copies eighteen rows of staged character codes into the chosen playfield screen page. Row pointers come from $480F and $4841, with columns wrapping within 64-byte source rows.
Low source byte in the staged character fetch. Selected from the row's low-byte directory at $480F.
High source byte of the character row fetch patched from the ring's row-address table at $4841.
Low destination operand of the visible character store. The row copy adds forty for each output row.
High byte of the self-modified screen destination operand at $0F2A. The copy loop backs up through the source columns, wrapping to 63, and advances the patched destination by forty for each new row.
Restarts the source column index at 63 on wrap and continues the row copy if any output columns remain.
Advances the patched screen destination by forty, decrements the rows remaining, and signals completion through $28FB after the last row.
Waits for the raster region at $0FBB, then copies the staged colour rows to colour RAM using the camera indices and row-pointer tables at $4873 and $48A5.
First address byte of the colour source operand in the instruction at $0F93. Both address bytes are set for each row by the row table loads.
High source byte of the colour row fetch patched from the row-address table at $48A5.
Low destination operand used by the colour row store. Updated together with the adjacent high byte at $0F98.
Patched high destination byte of the visible colour RAM row store. The copier advances the address by 40 for each row.
Waits until the hardware raster is between $4F and $C7 with the high raster bit clear.
Walks 18-byte slots starting after the player and clears their leading bytes until the $FF stop slot. Resets the active impact and projectile counters.
Offset where the projectile overlap scan begins. The main loop updates it before testing the active projectile slots.

Resumes scanning at a selected projectile slot. Tests eligible enemy records for relative X and Y overlap, clears the projectile on a hit, and dispatches through the patched jump from the target type's table entry at $1B10.
Patched low byte of the projectile-hit dispatch jump. It holds the selected object's callback from $1B10.
Patched high byte of the projectile-hit callback from $1B11.
Holds the originating projectile or object index for a collision handler reached through a patched jump.
Resets the projectile scan cursor to three. When damage is enabled, checks contact with live entity records and selects the type-specific handler through the address table at $1B3C.
Patched low address byte of the second collision dispatch jump at $10D3.
Patched high byte of the collision jump. After the jump site, the alternate path increments X by the eighteen-byte slot stride.

Scans the eight-byte records at $1151 and skips records outside the coarse camera window. Computes screen coordinates for each eligible record and patches the interaction call from the type's two bytes at $1B69.
Low byte of the room-interaction handler call selected from $1B69.
High byte of the room-interaction handler call selected from $1B6A. On return, the scan restores its index and moves to the next eight-byte entry.
Tail-jump back to the interaction scan after advancing eight bytes. The room save routine also indexes at $1149 so that its post-copy Y addresses the start of the record it just copied.
Room initialization copies records here in groups of eight. The first byte of a record is X, the second is Y, and the visible-entry scan stops on a negative X.
Second byte in the eight-byte interaction record. The cell lookup compares this row with the player's location.
Third byte of each interaction record. The dispatch code uses it to choose the routine from the interaction handler tables.
Fourth byte of each copied interaction record. The timed-spawn handler at $70F0 decrements it and reloads it when launching another object.
First byte of the four-byte argument group. The tile toggle increments it, and the spawn insertion at $7424 copies it as the new spawn column.
Second argument byte. $742A copies it as the spawn row, and the tile toggle stores the linked tile state here.
Third argument byte. $7430 copies it into the mutable third field of a new spawn record.
Fourth argument byte. $7436 copies it as the new spawn type. The following bytes carry the subsequent eight-byte working records.
Configuration 0 supplies 7 8-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $1151.
A second byte-for-byte copy of the six active eight-byte interaction records and their all-$FF terminator. The room directory points to the first copy.
Configuration 1 supplies 12 8-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $1151.
Eleven additional interaction records and an all-$FF terminator. Four handler-$20 entries carry a four-byte target tuple in the second half. The loader stops at the earlier terminator.
Configuration 2 supplies 15 8-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $1151.
Fourteen additional eight-byte interaction records and an all-$FF terminator. The loader stops at the earlier terminator, leaving these later grid coordinates and handler arguments in place.
Configuration 3 supplies 6 8-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $1151.
A second copy of five interaction records and an all-$FF terminator. The first two entries use handler key $06 and argument $28.
Configuration 4 supplies 9 8-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $1151.
Eight additional interaction records and an all-$FF terminator beyond the earlier terminator. Five of these rows use handler key $06 and argument $28.
First of two persistent target counters. Projectile damage at $2BFF reduces it and switches to the break path on borrow.
X coordinate of the first persistent target, used when placing its impact and replacing its room tile.
Y coordinate of the first target, used by the impact and destruction paths.
Second persistent target counter. The other damage case at $2BC7 subtracts the hit strength.
X coordinate of the second persistent target. Used for the four-cell replacement on destruction.
Y coordinate of the second persistent target. Loaded with its X before the impact and room redraw.
Five six-byte records selected by the room directory. Setup copies the selected record to $14E1 and room change writes its updated bytes back.
Five six-byte initial room state records copied to $14E7 by the reset routine at $0A44.

Walks the four-byte room spawn records at $15A0. For records in the camera window, converts tile coordinates to screen coordinates, finds an entity slot, and dispatches to the initializer selected by the record's type.
Patched low byte of the room spawn handler from the directory at $1AE4.
Patched high byte of the room spawn handler. The next path increments the table index four times before looking at another record.
Last of four increments of the spawn-list scan index. The room save also reads from $159C plus its post-copy index to inspect the first byte of the record just copied.
Room setup copies four-byte groups from the room configuration pointer until a group whose fourth byte is $FF.
Grid row in the four-byte spawn record. The room loader copies the record here from the selected directory.
Spawn flag that the object installers set to $FE after copying a spawn record into an active slot.
Fourth byte of each working spawn record. It selects the launch handler, with $FF as a record terminator for the room copy.
X column of the second spawn record. The insert path can write an all-$FF stop record at this next slot.
Y row of the second spawn record and second byte written when insertion advances the stop marker.
Third byte of the next four-byte spawn record. Filled with $FF when the previous slot has just been inserted.
Last byte of the next spawn record. The working lists continue with the same four-byte layout through $161F.
Configuration 0 supplies 5 4-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $15A0.
Collision address arithmetic retained between the two spawn lists. These 24 bytes agree with $1BDA and $1C34 and end in the first byte of an instruction cut off by the next list.
Second copy of the four active spawn records and their all-$FF terminator. The room directory selects the copy at $1620.

Retained terrain-test instructions after the second list. The common prefix with $1C06 checks the low coordinate nibble before reading a neighbouring tile and returning an attribute. This fragment uses $42BB as its indexed base.
Configuration 1 supplies 14 4-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $15A0.
Fragments of an indexed tile probe and page-pointer adjustment survive between the two room-one spawn lists. The next list overwrites the final instruction's operand.
Earlier version of the room-one spawn list. It shares its first five four-byte entries with the active copy at $1678. In the retained version the next pair uses grid column $17.
Bytes left behind from coordinate arithmetic like the code at $1C34. The fragment adds the camera offset to a coordinate and repeatedly shifts the two-byte result right.
Configuration 2 supplies 17 4-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $15A0.
Twenty-four bytes matching $1D5C–$1D73. In the complete routine this part increments the slot index by eighteen until it finds a vacant slot or a terminating $FF.
A second 17-entry copy of the room-two spawn list, including its terminator. Its middle and final coordinates differ from the active version at $1718.
A backward branch and return left after the retained room-two spawn entries, followed by zero bytes.
The bytes $01, $64 and $3C are the surviving start of a record in the gap before the next spawn list. Its consumer is open.
Configuration 3 supplies 21 4-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $15A0.
Distinct room-three spawn list in the same four-byte layout as $17D0. Grids differ and the list ends at an all-$FF record.
Configuration 4 supplies 5 4-byte records through the record ending in $FF. Room initialization copies this run to $15A0.
Calls the 50-iteration delay at $1EC1 and then repeats the loop using the equipment entry $7C6B, waiting at $223B each iteration.
Byte-for-byte copy of the four active room-four spawn records and their all-$FF terminator.
Begins with 23 bytes identical to the movement helper at $1EE8, testing the directional latches and storing signed motion requests. The next interaction routine starts at $1900.
With select held and a matching interaction available, queues the cue at $9039 and transfers control to the terminal entry at $6382.

Checks the select input and current interaction before choosing the target room offset. A live store probe at $1935 selects $7C3E for item three and zero for item four, with the previous offset saved at $09EC.

Copies four-byte spawn records from $15A0 and eight-byte interaction records from $1151 to the original room-specific destinations, using each final-byte terminator. Writes back six room state bytes from $14E1.

Configures the player and video for the transition, initializes the four-byte moving-object list at $B400 and runs a loop updating the controls and objects. Returns $FF if $1F09 is set during the sequence, otherwise returns zero after the counters expire.
Resets the engine display state at $0FD1, clears the transition flag and background override, and returns A zero.
Walks four-byte records at $B400 until a leading $FF. For active entries adds their two velocities, discards entries beyond either coordinate limit and calls $3DEE to render the remaining objects.
Saved list index reloaded after drawing the transition point. The following increment advances four bytes to the next point.
Clears three 240-byte runs in the selected screen bank. Also blanks three pages in one of the two character banks as selected by bit one of $1ADF.
Fills 21 raster charset choices from $1ADF before toggling its bit one and the screen selection bit in $0D47.
Current transition charset choice. Bit one toggles between the two banks used for the transition display.
Written by the transition screen-clearing path when it changes the active display content.
Set during the room-change script and cleared by the exit helper. The thrust effect renderer suppresses spawning while it is set.
Inner loop countdown for the transition's display and movement updates.
Outer loop countdown tested after the inner count reaches zero.
Little-endian addresses for spawn handlers. The scan at $1523 passes the type as a byte offset and copies the selected pair into its call operand.
High byte of the first spawn callback stored in the dispatch triplets. Other type values select their low and high pair through the corresponding dispatch site.
Little-endian callback addresses selected by entity type when the hit paths at $107D and $6247 dispatch through patched operands.
High byte of the first projectile-hit callback. $1083 reads it with the current slot's handler offset.
Callback addresses for the proximity test at $1093. The dispatch uses the slot type byte as an even offset and places the pair in the JMP at $10D3.
High byte of one of the collision callback lists. Each entry pairs a little-endian address with the low byte immediately preceding it.
Shared RTS handler used when a table entry has no action for the object's type.
Callback addresses indexed by the type in the eight-byte room interaction record. The handler address is copied into the instruction operand before the call.
High byte of the first handler in the room-interaction lookup beginning at $1B69.
Little-endian routine addresses indexed by the type byte at slot offset three. The loop at $1D8B copies the two bytes into its JMP operand at $1DAB.
High byte paired with $1B95 for the slot update dispatch. Each type is already an even byte offset, so the dispatch can use the type directly as the index.

Projects the entity's top edge into the room grid and looks up its tile attribute. If that attribute is zero and the slot crosses the X threshold within the tile, returns the neighbouring tile's attribute.
Uses the slot Y plus $15 to select a terrain row. Probes the next column if the first tile attribute is zero and the slot's X fraction reaches five.
Tests the tile at the entity's right edge, using X plus $0C. If the first tile attribute is zero and the vertical fraction reaches six, probes the tile in the following row.
Tests the tile at X minus one, clamped to zero before adding the camera offset. When the first tile attribute is zero and the vertical fraction reaches six, tests the following row.
Looks at three fixed 18-byte records before the regular object list. Returns X at an available slot with A zero, or the occupied leading value when all three are in use.
Searches from offset $48 in increments of eighteen. Returns A equal to $FF for a vacant slot, or X zero when it reaches the $FF list terminator.
Patches the absolute source with the pointer in A and Y. Copies eighteen bytes from that template into the object record indexed by X.
Mutable low byte of the template source address. $1D71 sets it just before copying the eighteen-byte object slot.
High byte of the template pointer patched from Y by $1D74. The copy consumes eighteen consecutive bytes through the patched operand.
Operand of the final LDX. The routine patches it with the initial destination slot index so that X is restored after copying.
Walks 18-byte records starting with the player. Skips zero records and stops on $FF. Looks up the object type at offset three and writes that routine's address into the jump at $1DAB.
Mutable low byte of the active object's update callback loaded from $1B95.
Patched high operand of the object-dispatch jump. The next entry at $1DAE clears the current slot, and $1DB3 advances to the next one.
Low byte of the camera-derived horizontal origin shared by slot-to-map coordinate conversions. The player world coordinate adds the player position to this offset.
High byte of the same camera-derived origin, added with carry when converting a slot's X.
Low byte of the world Y origin before doubling it for pixel-based collision and placement.
High byte of the world Y origin read when projecting a slot's leading edge onto a map row.
Doubled low origin byte used by paths that require the game's higher vertical coordinate scale.
High byte of the doubled vertical camera origin.
Next index for a queued object when writing screen coordinates, shape and colour before raster scheduling.
Player vertical position. The thrust path executes two decrements with a clear collision bit.
Right movement increments this byte by one. The sprite renderer doubles the X coordinate for VIC pixels.
Vertical screen coordinate in each non-player slot. The drawing path copies it to the raster sprite list and the collision probes use it to find the object's room row.
Object type at offset three. The dispatch at $1D9B looks up the update callback using this byte.
The projectile test picks up the hit strength from this byte. For damageable room objects, hit handlers instead subtract the incoming strength from it.
Bit six permits the slot to participate in the projectile overlap test at $1033.
Upper limit used by the projectile overlap check for the slot's relative X distance.
Upper limit used by the projectile overlap check for relative Y distance.
Field at offset eight. A patrol uses it as its room column for the visibility test. The chasing handler instead adjusts it as a signed velocity.
Field at offset nine. The patrol uses it as its room row. The chasing callback stores the other signed velocity here.
First callback-private phase byte. In the impact animation it is the countdown to the next frame. The timed projectile instead uses it as its horizontal step.
Second callback-private byte. The impact callback reloads its frame counter from here, while the bouncing projectile uses it as horizontal velocity.
Third callback-private byte. The bouncing projectile uses it as signed vertical velocity during its movement and reflection checks.
Fourth callback-private byte. For the bouncing projectile it is the remaining lifetime. The room chasing callback also updates this field during movement.
The chase handler uses this field to gate contact and hit handling when the sprite is visible. The patrol can also use it as a countdown.
Offset fifteen. The chasing handler increments it and uses its low bits to pace changes to the velocity.
Offset sixteen. Supplies the current frame choice to the chasing handler, which replaces it with the next animation index.
Offset seventeen of the player slot. The patrol's equivalent byte holds a signed movement step. Thirteen fixed-size object records start at $1DC2 and advance eighteen bytes per slot.
An all-$FF record at the end of the active slot list. The dispatcher tests the leading byte before considering any other field in the slot.
Calls $1EC1 then falls through into the same delay a second time after the call returns.
Loops fifty times, checking equipment selection and waiting at $223B on each pass. Keeps its loop count on the stack across the calls.
Eight VIC colour codes appearing alongside the transition wait helper. Their order matches a run in the title colour table at $074E.
Clears both movement requests, samples configured inputs and sets the applicable signed request to plus or minus four for each held direction.
Set when the death path begins. The player update ages it before choosing the next restart or title path.
Remaining invulnerability or damage delay checked before the next hit can drain the panel gauge.
Hit strength copied from the projectile slot before the target's damage handler is dispatched.
Uses a zero-initialized eight-bit count to wait at $223B 256 times before entering the title return path at $08D9.
Manages the input lock timers, tests terrain before horizontal movement, then applies thrust or gravity through separate vertical probes.
At the right edge's horizontal alignment, finds the neighbouring map tile and looks up its attributes. A second row is tested if the first attribute is zero and the player spans rows.
At the left edge's horizontal alignment, checks the neighbouring tile and a possible second row before allowing left movement.
Accumulates the contact attributes returned by the adjacent movement probes.
Checks the map row below Dan when vertically aligned. It combines attributes from a second column when the sprite spans the boundary.
Computes the row above Dan and tests one or two map columns against the attribute table.
In normal play, applies camera compensation and selects a three-sprite group from movement, facing and animation state. A nonzero $1AE1 bypasses compensation and takes the fixed $FC group.
Builds three sprite positions from the player coordinates and the selected offsets. It writes the two upper X bits to slots at $291B and $291C and prepares their colours.
Byte read during player sprite pose selection before the title-specific raster wait entry.
Updates the title twinkle cells at $0845, then falls through to the common raster wait at $223B.
Clears the synchronization byte at $0D37 and waits for a raster interrupt to change it.
Reads CIA 1 port A once and masks the five active-low joystick lines into the shared input latches.
Saves the last select and fire values. A nonzero $1B selects joystick port 2, and zero selects the configured keyboard.
Rotates a zero through eight row selects on CIA 1 port A and stores each port B sample in $22CC–$22D3.
Eight bytes written by the full matrix scan. The scan forces bit 7 of the second byte high.
Result returned from the second sampled keyboard row. The menu tests bit zero here when selecting the controller.
Last byte of the keyboard row scan. The title menu tests bits zero and three, and the pause handler tests bit seven.
Eight masks used by the multiplexing code to set a selected sprite's high X bit.
Complementary masks used by the scheduler to clear a selected sprite's high X bit.
Acknowledges raster IRQ, decrements the sync byte and runs the audio update. It checks CIA 2 bit 2 before restoring registers.
Selects the branch in $2307 that services music or gameplay audio.
Tail-jumps to $AC0C for a nonzero mode or $AE50 when the mode is zero.
Chooses a delay from $2598 according to the count in X and waits for the beam to pass raster $BC before switching display modes.
Uses an opcode patched from $2598 and a run of NOPs to time the writes that switch the lower display to bitmap mode.
Counts sprites near the split, then selects a raster wait path using $0D4C. Both paths switch the lower display to bitmap mode.
Uses an opcode patched from $25A1 followed by NOPs before setting the lower display registers and acknowledging the raster interrupt.
Runs the audio tick and writes sprite slots 1–7 from their arrays to the VIC registers and to both sprite pointer tables.
Subtracts the two direction-specific deltas indexed by $0D13 from each five-byte screen object record. Clears the pending move flag at $0D12.
First component of the scroll displacement pair indexed by the saved scroll direction.
Signed Y displacement for the first scroll direction. Each movement entry provides the X byte at $2473 plus the direction offset and the Y byte one address later.
Returns while the terminal display is active. Otherwise it processes scroll compensation and advances the sprite update bookkeeping.

Clears the previous marker if its screen code is at least $F9. Resolves the current screen row and column from the indexed record and writes the new marker over an empty cell or another marker. Stores the address for the next erase.
When $24 and $1AE1 are zero, searches five-byte slots for a free marker. Derives a screen column and row from Dan's coordinates and facing, initializes the marker to $F9, and sets $2569 to four.
Animation phase used to decide when the jet effect advances to the next glyph.
Delay byte set when a fresh thrust effect enters a free display slot.
Column of a visible jet effect cell, initialized from the player's X and facing direction.
Row of a visible jet effect cell derived from the player's vertical screen position.
Zero is free. An active slot starts at screen code $F9. The timer advances that code and the draw helper limits where it can replace screen cells.
Low byte of the previous screen cell used by this effect. The draw path saves it for the next update.
High byte of the previous screen cell address, completing each five-byte jet effect record.
Raster split adjustment indexed by the number of sprites near the boundary. The lower display handler reads it at $2312.
Alternate split delay indexed by the boundary sprite count when the fine-scroll condition takes the path at $237D.
Preserves A and X and ORs $0C into the precomputed screen selection, selecting the bank at $F000. Continues with raster acknowledgment.
Preserves A and X and ORs $0A into the precomputed screen selection, selecting the bank at $E800. Continues with raster acknowledgment.
Saves A and X, selects the charset with bit 3 set in the buffered $D018 value, and advances the raster sequence.
Compares consecutive charset select values at $2735 and dispatches each change to $2635 with a row index in Y.
Queued raster lines for the charset switch events spliced into the upcoming sprite schedule.
Queued handler numbers parallel to the charset raster lines, with a negative value ending the list.
Preserves the caller's X and Y by patching reload operands. Chooses a charset handler using the room's raster charset list and queues a switch when the calculated raster line is below $B8.
Saved Y operand used to calculate the new raster line. The routine multiplies the band index by 32 and adds the adjusted fine-scroll offset.
Saved X operand restored before returning from the insertion of the charset switch.
Number of charset switch events queued while building the upcoming raster sequence.
Offset formed by inverting and doubling the camera's fine Y phase for raster line calculation.
Charset schedule index loaded before the first D018 write in the playfield IRQ.
Counts sprites 1–7 whose Y coordinates fall in the unsigned interval $A8 through $C0, inclusive.
Playfield background colour written by the IRQ. The flash timer alternates a replacement colour here.
Sets both fine-scroll registers from camera state, selects the playfield screen and charset, and programs the next raster interrupt.
Acknowledges VIC IRQ, advances the slot, and wraps at a negative table entry. It writes the next raster line and IRQ vector before restoring registers and returning.
Charset selection bytes indexed by the coarse camera row and used to update $D018 across the playfield.
The comparison at $25E7 adds the camera index to this address to inspect the row after the currently selected row at $2735,X.
The same runtime row list viewed two entries ahead of the initial camera index. $25F4 checks whether a new charset is needed here.
Array position read three rows ahead of the initial camera index by the raster schedule setup.
Runtime charset lookup for the fourth row after the initial camera-indexed entry.
Remainder of the room's per-row charset list. The scheduler can compare later rows by indexing this same contiguous list from $2735 onward.
VIC raster compare table, indexed by the current raster slot.
Low bytes of IRQ entry addresses, indexed by the handler selector.
Entry two of the raster handler address-low table. The room setup installs it as the first IRQ address.
High bytes of IRQ entry addresses, paired with the low bytes at $2764.
Entry two of the raster handler address-high table, installed together with its low byte during setup.
Maps raster slots to handler indices. The cycling IRQ recognizes a negative byte as the wrap marker.
Remaining handler type indices after the start of the raster dispatch sequence. Negative values restart the schedule.

Raster dispatch target for slot seven. Saves A and X, takes the next object from the $297B link array and uploads coordinates, the shared high-X register, shape pointer and colour before advancing the raster schedule at $2708.
Uploads the next scheduled object into hardware sprite six and writes its pointer in both screen matrices before entering $2708.
Uploads the next scheduled object into hardware sprite five and writes its pointer in both screen matrices before entering $2708.
Uploads the next scheduled object into hardware sprite four and writes its pointer in both screen matrices before entering $2708.
Uploads the next scheduled object into hardware sprite three and writes its pointer in both screen matrices before entering $2708.
Uploads the next scheduled object into hardware sprite two and writes its pointer in both screen matrices before entering $2708.
Uploads the next scheduled object into hardware sprite one and writes its pointer in both screen matrices before entering $2708.
Resets $D0 and $30 before the next drawing pass.
Seeds the visible sprite list head at $D0 with 1, makes object 1 link to 2 at $D1, terminates object 2's link at $D2 and sets the visible count at $30 to 2.
Low X byte in the first reserved player-piece slot of the multiplexing queue.
Low X byte for the second reserved player drawing entry.
X low byte for the last reserved player sprite. Subsequent entries carry the other queued sprites.
High X bit for the first reserved player piece, paired with $290A.
High X bit for the second reserved player piece, paired with $290B.
Ninth X bit for the third reserved player sprite. The matching low byte is stored at $290C.
Indexed low X coordinates written to the VIC by the later raster handlers for sprites one through seven.
Screen Y positions for the next scheduled uploads.
Prepared values for $D010. The raster handlers update the shared high-X bits along with individual sprite positions.
Four values indexed by the rifle projectile collision handler when choosing the impact response.
Sprite shape pointers in raster order. The handlers write matching pointer bytes to both matrices.
VIC colour values installed by the mid-frame sprite upload handlers.
Link to the next queued sprite entry. Each raster sprite handler loads this value before updating its slot.
First vertical offset field in the pose's three-piece lookup group.
Middle vertical offset field in the pose table.
Third Y delta in each three-byte pose record. The player renderer adds it to the player's Y and fine vertical display offset.
First piece's colour selector in each player pose record.
Middle colour field in each pose group.
Third colour field in the pose table used by the player renderer.
Horizontal offset for the first piece in the player's pose group.
Horizontal offset for the middle piece in the same pose layout.
Third horizontal offset in each pose's three-byte group. The renderer adds it to the player's half-pixel X coordinate.
Fills unused entries in the temporary sprite assignment list, then appends the queued charset switches and their raster line bytes. A negative handler value terminates the queue.

Walks the linked list headed at $D0 to fill the first hardware sprite slots. Holds additional X, Y, pointer, colour and X-high values in raster update arrays, and calls $2ABE to schedule a slot change.
Saved head value at the linked-sprite scheduling code. The transfer beginning at $2AAD copies the current link from the temporary zero-page list to $297B.
Saves X and Y, computes a raster position from this object's Y plus $16, and uses $2AD6 to splice in pending charset switches before restoring the caller's registers.
Reload operand holding X across the raster event insertion.
Reload operand holding Y across the same insertion. $2AC1 patches this byte before replacing Y with the current object number.
Places a pending charset transition before the next sprite update when their raster lines are close, then appends the sprite update when it lies above the panel limit.
Proposed scanline saved before pending charset events are inserted.

Adds the fine-scroll deltas, doubles the indexed object's horizontal coordinate, and writes its sprite pointer, colour and coordinates to the staging arrays. Inserts the new index into the list sorted by Y and advances the staging index.
Saves the selector, shape and screen coordinates to the current draw slot. Doubles X for the VIC and inserts the slot index into the linked list at $D0 using Y as the sort key.
First shape-pointer slot in the visible object list. Player pose logic and ordinary object drawing share this table.
Sprite shape pointer of the second reserved player drawing entry.
Third reserved player sprite's shape byte. Later entries use the same location within the visible shape array.
Colour slot at the head of the visible object list used for sprite scheduling.
The middle reserved player piece's colour used by the multiplex scheduler.
Third reserved player's piece colour. The final piece uses the colour index read by $2228 from the pose data.
Uses attribute bit one to select one of two tile-damage counters and subtracts the slot's hit strength. On borrow prepares the replacement cells and calls the effect and award routines.
Clears the upper pair of room cells and continues into $2C4D, which clears the two pairs beneath them.
Increments the row first, then clears two adjacent cells in that row and two more in the next row.
Writes tile zero and refreshes four cells in a two-by-two pattern, advancing the room column and row between calls.
Resolves the descriptor for tile zero and the room cell pointer for the requested position. Replaces the cell with zero, refreshes its staged screen and colour data, and queues its position.
Writes the requested tile at $414E, resolves its metatile allocations and updates the staged playfield character and colour data for the affected cell.
Mutable operand holding the assigned tile index returned by $414E. The following loop uses it to look up the tile's staged glyphs.
Looks for the sign-bit terminator in the two-byte coordinate list starting at $2D3F. Writes the requested pair before installing a new terminator.
Skips updates while a camera update is pending. Walks two-byte entries until a negative first byte and passes each coordinate to $2CCF.
Converts a room tile coordinate into staging and visible screen offsets, then asks $2D4D to update four character rows and their colours.
Coordinate pairs consumed by $2CAF. The consumer invalidates the queue by writing the terminator into its first byte.
High byte of a queued room tile address, paired with the low byte at $2D3F.
Beginning of the second queue entry. The writer places a negative low byte here when it appends the preceding pointer.
Invokes the pointer-increment drawing wrapper three times before falling through for the fourth subcolumn.
Draws through $2D60 and advances three column pointers to the adjacent subcolumn.
Clips the destination column and row, chooses a playfield page from $0D47, and copies the staged character and colour to their separate destinations.
Uses tile coordinates to compute a character and colour buffer offset, then writes four rows of four character codes to the staging buffer at $9A00 and four rows of colour values at $B400.
Stores four source bytes one row apart in the descriptor planes, then advances the destination to the next 64-byte row.
Advances the descriptor pointer by $40 and the destination pointer by one, carrying into each high byte.
Low offset byte added to the bitmap glyph pointer for each text row.
High offset byte added after the low-byte addition and its carry.
Draws the panel glyph when its horizontal position begins on the other half of a bitmap byte. Splits the source nibbles across destination cells and advances the horizontal cursor by three.
Patched immediate X reloaded as the text renderer returns.
Start of the scratch addressing base also used at offset eight for the already shifted first half of a bitmap glyph.
Eight row bytes temporarily holding the shifted nibbles from the first half of a bitmap glyph. The renderer merges these with existing destination pixels.
Copies a 16-byte glyph to the panel bitmap, preserving the neighbouring nibble. Odd horizontal positions use the shifted path at $2E35.
Reload operand holding the first saved bitmap text input register.
Reload operand holding the second saved bitmap text input register.
Computes a panel bitmap pointer from the horizontal half-cell and the row tables at $2E25 and $2E2D.
Multiplies the glyph index by 16 and adds base $4A14 to form its source pointer.
Converts Dan's position to coarse room coordinates and compares both axes with the eight-byte interaction record selected by Y. Returns zero on a match within the two tested positions on each axis.

Scans keyboard row seven. Matrix key row seven, column seven reached $2F59 with a clear high bit, while the released control returned at $2F6F. The pause path waits for release before polling for a resume input.
Reads the stream at A/X. Bytes below $80 go to the glyph renderer. $DF consumes row and column operands, and $DC/$DD enter and repeat a loop.
A jump whose operand selects the title renderer or one of the gameplay text renderers.
Patched low address byte of the text renderer jump. The text mode setter selects which character drawing path receives the next glyph.
Patched high address byte of the text renderer jump selected by $7F96.
Saves the character byte and jumps directly to the shared draw path at $3056. $7F8F installs this entry in the text dispatch jump.
Saves the character byte and increments $308A. Every fourth character it waits at $223B and checks equipment input while preserving the stream pointer and cursor variables. Then continues into $3056.
Converts a stream byte to a screen character by subtracting $40, writes it to the selected screen page and applies the configured colour.
Colour value last requested by the text stream and written by the active text renderer.
Character counter. Its low two bits select when the gameplay text renderer waits for the raster and samples equipment.
Draws a tall character with $30A5. M and W append an extra column using special character codes $5B and $5C.
Converts the text byte to two consecutive screen codes for vertically stacked tiles and draws both at the current column.
Twenty-four low bytes of the text screen row pointers. Both single-row and double-height text drawing use them.
High bytes of the text row pointers in the first matrix, before drawing adjusts them for the other screen or colour RAM.
Forty low bytes of eight-times-column offsets through $0138. The sequence wraps to zero at column 32.
High bytes for the 40 eight-byte cell offsets. The entries are zero through column 31 and one for the final eight columns.
Increments the little-endian pointer at $02/$03, carrying into $03 when the low byte wraps.
Increments the little-endian pointer at $0A/$0B, carrying into $0B when $0A wraps.
Advances the address in $0C/$0D by one byte and leaves the high byte alone until the low byte wraps.
Advances the destination at $04/$05 and leaves its high byte alone unless the low byte wraps.
Adds one to the little-endian address at $06/$07, incrementing $07 on low-byte overflow.
Steps the little-endian source address at $08/$09 forward by one byte.
Subtracts one from the little-endian counter at $15/$16 while preserving A. The returned flags include the flags from restoring A with PLA.
Subtracts one from the pointer at $06/$07 while saving and restoring A.
Copies twenty 40-byte rows through the source at $02 and destination at $04. Advances source an additional 24 bytes after each row, making the source stride 64.
Saves A, checks the flag at $0844 and jumps to title setup if it is nonzero. Otherwise it restores A and returns from the interrupt.
Mutes SID and scans the keyboard. A clear bit seven in the tested row returns to the title, while the other path jumps through $0200.
An absolute jump back to its own opcode, forming a three-byte spin loop.
Clears the raster slot and synchronization byte, writes raster $C6, and installs the IRQ vector from handler table index 2.
Writes raster $DC and installs the title interrupt at $22E4 with IRQ disabled during the update.
The first 32 terrain metatiles, each made of sixteen little-endian glyph indices in 4 by 4 row order. $45DC scales the metatile number by 32 before $46F1 reads the words.
Metatiles 32–63. The last metatile's glyph indices reach 632, the final glyph compacted by startup.

When $0D14 is set, clears the old four-cell markers and uses $0B7D/$0B7E divided by four as the new position. Clears eight bytes at $C7B8 and sets one bit from the low three bits of each coordinate divided by eight.
One bit per column, from bit 7 at column zero to bit 0 at column seven.
Wraps the record coordinates modulo 20 and 9 and saves the computed screen pointer. Tries four cells, with twenty screen bytes between the columns and 360 bytes between the rows.
Writes screen code $F7 through the pointer at $C0 plus Y when the existing code is zero.
Nine little-endian row addresses at forty-byte increments starting at $C800. The caller also folds in the screen page bit derived from $0D48.
High bytes of the marker's screen row addresses. The draw path adds the active matrix's bank adjustment.
Reloads the previous screen pointer from the record at X and checks the four cells used by the marker routine.
Zeros the screen code addressed by $C0 and Y when it is $F7 or $F8.
Six bytes used as X-indexed state for the saved screen pointer and the wrapped marker coordinates.
Saved low address byte used when the marker cleanup restores the prior position.
Marker grid X after shifting the camera's logical column by two. Bounds handling wraps it before the screen cell is addressed.
Marker grid Y derived from the camera's logical row. The update constrains it to the panel marker grid.
Derives coordinates via $7F9D, patches the record at $3BFD with those coordinates, then copies it to a free entity slot if $1D59 finds one.
Saved slot-index byte in the close-chaser spawn path's register restore.

Moves the signed velocity components toward the player, limiting X to one unit either way and Y to four. Adds the resulting velocity to the entity position, queues draw selector $0E, and advances the slot loop.
Calls $9019, zeros the entity's active byte, and increments $7C3C. On count five copies six bytes from $7C59 to $7C37. Advances $7C3E across five offsets spaced $11 apart.
Fourteen explicit initializer bytes. The spawn routine replaces the position bytes at offsets one and two before $1D71 copies the record into a slot.
First screen coordinate stored in the close chaser slot initializer before it is copied.
Second screen coordinate stored by the close chaser initializer. The remaining parameters describe the slot's initial type and motion.
Copies the source slot's coordinates into the initializer at $3E55 and asks $1D71 to copy it to the slot index returned by $1D59.
Saved slot-index byte restored after the current room object update.

While its timer is nonzero, adds two to its size, saves half the size, and draws the outline. On expiry compares the player with the final bounds and removes the slot, with sound and a call to $6A84 on the outside path.
Uses the slot position plus or minus its size to call the horizontal edge renderer twice and the vertical renderer twice. Restores the slot index from a patched immediate.
Saved slot-index byte reloaded after updating the room object's temporary screen coordinates.

Plots a vertical multicolour line of twice the incoming length. Divides the X coordinate to select a cell and pixel mask, allocates a glyph for an empty screen cell, and ORs each mask into the glyph row.
Plots a horizontal line. Uses per-pixel masks until aligned, writes $FF for complete groups of four pixels, then plots the remainder.
Reads the screen cell under the supplied X coordinate and allocates a glyph from $1AE0 if empty. Forms its eight-byte glyph address using the active charset selector at $1ADF.
Bounds-checks the row and column, allocates a glyph for an empty cell, and ORs in the two-bit mask corresponding to the subcell X coordinate. Returns $FF outside the playfield.
Four masks isolate the successive two-bit pixels in a multicolour character row.
Initializer used by $3C0B. Offsets one and two are patched with the source coordinates. Type $26 selects the update routine at $3C27.
X coordinate placed in the transition object template by $3C11.
Y coordinate placed in that template by $3C17, followed by the object's type and initial callback state.
Calls the slot allocator at $1D59 and passes the initializer at $3F53 to the record copier at $1D71.

On timer underflow, spawns the expanding entity, reloads a five-step timer, and chooses a nonzero velocity distinct from the pair it computed by negating the old velocity. Bounds tests force components inward near the edges. Adds the selected velocity and allocates a trailing particle.
Searches four-byte records at $B400 for a zero first byte, stopping on $FF. Writes the slot position and two even velocity components, rerolling when both are zero.
Explicit initializer bytes passed to the slot copier at $3E63. Type $24 selects update routine $3E6D.
Adds the current camera deltas at $0B3D/$0B3E to the entity's two stored coordinates.
Temporarily offsets the entity position by $10 and $33 for the draw call at $2B26, then restores the original coordinates adjusted by the camera deltas.
Saved return value for the temporary object draw at $3F8F. The tail restores the slot coordinates with the two movement deltas applied.
Resets camera and transition state, reads a room configuration, copies its object records, and expands its map and character data.
Expands the stream to $A600. $F8 emits a run of zeroes, $F9 repeats a supplied tile byte and $FF ends the stream.
Scans three-byte entries through the pointer at $4C for the map address in $04/$05 or a negative terminator. Writes that address and the incoming A, restoring Y on return.
Patched immediate value preceding the indirect room-record store at $4176. The following routine at $417B reads triples from the configuration pointer.
Immediate Y restore operand patched when the coordinate override routine starts.
Reads X, Y and tile triples until a negative X. $4192 resolves each coordinate and immediately stores the tile to the expanded map at $419C.
Saves Y while applying the tile change, then restores the override index to let the reader continue.
Saved override-record index for the final LDY immediately before returning to the room coordinate override loop.
Writes A into consecutive charset-select slots starting at X. Positive Y is the count. Zero wraps and produces 256 stores. The room configuration supplies positive counts.
Offset into the room build descriptors at $48E8. The charset builder saves it before the copy and uses it to fetch the corresponding map section.
Saved destination bank page, reused when building the terrain glyphs for the selected charset.
Prepares one of the room's three charset bands. Its arguments include the room pointer group and destination high byte.
On the first bank build only advances the bank-pass counter. On later passes, walks the previous 64-cell row and reserves the four border glyph codes used by each metatile.
Reads the four screen codes in the bottom row of a four-by-four metatile and marks their glyph slots occupied for the next build.
Marks the glyph slot named in A as occupied by writing $FF to its entry in the allocation page at $9E00.
Patches the source high byte from A and the destination high byte from X, then copies eight pages in order. Room setup calls this before it allocates and populates the band's variable glyphs.
Mutable high address byte of the source for the eight-page charset copier.
High destination byte in the self-modifying eight-page copy. It starts at the destination bank's high byte and advances after each page.
One initial attribute per source metatile. $43B2 looks it up before translating that metatile to its allocated runtime code.
Indexed attributes tested by movement and projectile collision probes. $43BF writes the source metatile attribute into the entry indexed by its allocated screen tile code.
Runs the reuse pass across the specified portion of the expanded map. The per-cell helper tries to preserve the prior bank's assigned index.
For a nonzero map cell, checks the previous allocation table. If assigned, installs that index in the new table and reserves the matching sixteen glyph slots.
Marks an already assigned screen code in the glyph occupancy table. Preserves the caller's metatile quadrant count.
Saved quadrant loop index restored after reserving a previously assigned glyph slot.
Traverses the tiles at $08/$09 for the byte count in $15/$16, marking the four glyphs in each tile's bottom row as reserved through $437F.
Indexes four code tables beginning at $9500 using tile A. Their entries select four occupied character slots in $9E00.
Marks the occupancy byte for glyph A at $9E00 with $FF and preserves the incoming X.

Scans the expanded band's tiles. For each tile it uses $45B4 to obtain the band-local tile index, then transfers the source tile's collision attribute to that index and replaces the original map byte with the remapped index.
Patched immediate attribute copied from the source metatile before the store to the new runtime code's attribute entry.
Sets the initial player and camera coordinates before rendering the first visible screen, then reads map data starting at $A600.
Copies the sixteen screen glyph codes and sixteen colours for metatile A from $9200–$99FF into matching 4 by 4 regions of the character and colour staging buffers.
First precomputed glyph or colour lookup index for a visible metatile strip. The later transfer uses this value in X.
Lookup index for the second cell of the strip.
Saved glyph/colour lookup index for the third strip cell.
Last lookup index prepared for the four-cell transfer.
Clears the four-page source glyph lookup, moves the current 64 allocation indices to the previous table and clears the occupancy page with slot zero reserved.
Clears two 64-byte remap arrays, resets the allocator to one and initializes the $9E00 buffer with a leading $FF.
Tracks whether room setup has begun its previous-row preservation passes. The first pass advances it without preserving another row.
Reuses the tile's existing index if present, otherwise assigns the next index and populates the tile's lookup columns.
Advances the little-endian descriptor index at $1C/$1D, carrying into its high byte on wrap.
Resolves the sixteen glyphs of metatile Y and stores the allocated screen codes and source colours in the parallel $9200 and $9600 tables at index X.
Reads one per-glyph colour byte from $0200 using the original glyph index in $1E/$1F and the caller's Y offset.

Reads the original glyph index selected by $1C/$1D from $322D. Returns its existing screen code when allocated. Otherwise copies eight rows into a free glyph slot in the charset selected by $17, and saves the slot index in the cache at $9A00 plus the original glyph index.
Scans the occupancy array for a zero entry, marks it occupied and saves the new character code.
Increments when the builder assigns a new metatile slot in the current charset.
Character index found in the glyph occupancy scan and returned to the source glyph lookup map.
Sixty-four entries recording allocated metatile indices for the bank being built. $45B7 checks this table before allocating, and $456E copies it to $47CF on switching banks.
Sixty-four allocation indices saved by $456E when the builder moves to another bank. $4335 tries these saved indices to preserve metatiles across the change.
Fifty low-byte addresses joining the high bytes at $4841. Scroll drawing patches its source operand from these two lists.
High bytes for the staged character row pointers, spanning $9A00 through $A1FF for the 32-row ring with repeated entries for wraparound.
Fifty low-byte addresses for the row pointers used when transferring staged colour bytes to colour RAM.
High bytes for the staged colour row pointers. The underlying ring runs from $B400 to $BBFF.
Writes zero through three overlapping indexed stores covering colour RAM $D800–$DACF.
Low start pointer byte for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 1.
High start pointer byte for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 1.
Low byte of the expanded cell count for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 1.
High byte of the expanded cell count for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 1.
Low start pointer byte for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 2.
High start pointer byte for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 2.
Low byte of the expanded cell count for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 2.
High byte of the expanded cell count for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 2.
Low start pointer byte for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 3.
High start pointer byte for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 3.
Low byte of the expanded cell count for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 3.
High byte of the expanded cell count for the expanded map slice used to build terrain charset band 3.
Low address byte of the compressed map stream in each 17-byte setup record.
High address byte paired with the compressed terrain pointer.
Counts rows assigned to the first charset and selects the first map section size.
Row count for the second charset band's expanded map traversal.
Final band row count for the third terrain charset.
Right movement bounds value copied to $0D45.
Lower movement limit loaded into $0D46 during room setup.
First byte of a room record points to the four-byte object data groups copied to $15A0.
High pointer byte for the room's four-byte spawn records.
Low address byte for the room's eight-byte interaction record source.
High byte of the interaction records pointer in the 17-byte setup record.
Low byte pointing to the room's six saved target-state bytes.
High byte selecting the source of the current room's target-state bytes.
Low address of the room's mutable coordinate and tile overrides.
High address of the per-room override list passed in $4C/$4D.
Starting camera column copied to the logical room coordinates at room setup.
Final byte of configuration zero, read as the room's initial camera row. More records of the same 17-byte format follow.
Compressed terrain pointer $8239, with working spawn and interaction sources at $1678 and $1241.
Compressed terrain pointer $83BB for the 24-row map. Selects spawn records at $1718 and interaction records at $1301.
Compressed terrain pointer $862D for the other 24-row map. The spawn and interaction records start at $17D0 and $13F1.
Fifth 17-byte room setup record. Points to the compressed terrain at $87E6 and the spawn and interaction lists at $18A8 and $1451.
Sixth room setup record used when $0953 writes $55 to the configuration offset. Reuses the map and object pointers of configuration zero with a different initial coordinate pair, $00 and $01.
Coordinate and tile override triples for the first map, with negative X terminating the list. Room reset fills its first byte with $FF.
Room-one persistent coordinate overrides. The room directory passes this address to the override reader and writer.
Room-two stored tile replacements. $414E can replace a matching triple or append at the first negative X.
Room-three coordinate override buffer. The first byte is reset to $FF when the game initializes its room state.
Last override list. It reserves the bytes up to the map pointer helper at $49F5.
Takes a row count in A, returns the corresponding byte length in $06/$07, and advances the destination at $04/$05 by $40 for each row.
Base of the 16-byte glyph records used by the panel bitmap renderer.
The first 128 resident eight-byte glyph images created when the entry routine compacts the nine-byte source records. $46F1 copies requested glyphs into a room charset.
Compact glyphs 128–255, addressed by the two-byte indices in the metatile definitions at $322D.
Glyphs 256–383. The charset allocation code multiplies each index by eight to find its first bitmap row.
Terrain glyphs 384–511, eight consecutive bitmap rows per image.
The 121 glyphs numbered 512–632 complete the compact terrain charset. Their colours are stored in the separate plane at $0200.
The untranslated tail of the original interleaved terrain records. Entry routine $A056 reads their bitmap and colour bytes as it compacts the full source into two separate planes.
Copies two overlapping spans of panel colours into colour RAM and sets the two multicolour backgrounds.
Timer for the timed screen-effect item. Its low bit controls whether the playfield's background colour is replaced.
Counts the flash timer down and alternates the background override at $26CE between zero and $0C.
Patched low byte of the effect trigger's indirect dispatch call at $6258.
Patched high byte of the effect trigger's selected handler. The follow-up restores the previous object index saved on the stack.
