Tests the previous fire sample and the selected item stock at $7C0D. If available, consumes one unit, starts the $6221 timer at $32 and invokes the sound and equipment display updates.

Fourteen explicit initializer bytes precede the launch routine at $628E. $628E patches the coordinates and X direction, then $1D71 copies eighteen bytes, including four from the following instructions.
Horizontal screen launch coordinate copied from the player's X position.
Vertical position of the bouncing projectile. The launcher rounds the player's Y down to an even number and adds two.
Signed horizontal step selected according to facing and written into the template before spawning.

Checks the prior fire sample, stock at $7BFD and slot availability. Consumes a unit, patches the launch coordinates and facing direction into $6280, installs the projectile and updates the equipment display.

Advances X and Y using signed velocities and probes terrain in the direction of each movement. On selected collision outcomes reverses and reapplies the corresponding velocity. Runs the expiry effect at $6B21 when the lifetime runs out.
Gates the normal playfield sprite update while the terminal has changed the display.
Saves the active charset table, switches to the terminal display, prints the menu stream at $65E6 and polls selection and fire.
Waits at $8000, then compares $7C17 with five. Controlled instruction stops reached the insufficient-fuel message path for four and the ending path for five. The ending prints the stream at $66D5.

Checks the current bomb supply before attempting a 150-unit debit through $659F. On success adds ten bombs, up to 99. A watch at $64E4 caught a change from zero to ten with a balance of 200 reduced to 50.
Adds five decimal digits from the record ending at $655B plus Y to the digit array at $7C48. Carries toward the more significant digits when a sum reaches ten.

First subtracts the five price digits without storing them. Returns $FF at $65CA on borrow. On success performs the subtraction again, normalizes the digits and stores the balance before returning zero.
Encoded menu stream reached by $63C9. It interleaves readable text with commands consumed by $2F70.
Encoded terminal heading, in upper-case PETSCII with $40 used as spacing.
Select-option prompt in the text stream.
Adds a six-byte digit sequence in reverse order to the panel counter at $6951, reducing each result modulo ten. Restores X from a patched immediate.
Patched byte that restores the caller's X after adding the six inventory digits.
Controls the sequence of digit updates at $6936. The inventory addition initializes it to six.
Decimal digit operands consumed by the inventory counter's six-byte modulo-ten addition at $68E5. A caller selects the last digit in Y.
Zeros six bytes at $6951–$6956 and calls the draw path once per slot.
Returns immediately with no redraw pending. Otherwise decrements the slot counter and draws the indexed tile.
Decrements the panel item count and computes its three-column slot position. Redraws that slot from the character indexed at $6951.
High address byte of the inventory redraw call just before the six displayed inventory cells.
Six decimal digits of the stored inventory panel value, indexed by the add and redraw paths.
Sets $6A5A to four and enters its panel redraw.
Draws the current count and pads the four-slot display with the alternate tile.
Repeats the panel draw operation with both icon selectors zero, saving the iteration count on the stack across each draw.
Enters the common inventory draw at $6988 using bitmap index $20 and colour index four.

Selects a bitmap destination from $04 and copies two groups of sixteen bytes from $6A0A indexed by A. Then uses the incoming Y to update four screen colour bytes and four colour RAM cells for the selected panel slot.
Saved X operand restored after the inventory icon transfer writes the bitmap and its colours.
Low bytes of the inventory bitmap destinations selected by the current icon slot.
Matching high bytes of the inventory icon destination pointers.
Per-slot offset applied to the four bitmap screen-matrix and four colour RAM fields.
Two 32-byte icon records. The copy at $699F takes sixteen bytes for the first two bitmap cells and $69B7 takes sixteen for the next row.
Combined bitmap colours for the top-left cell of a two-by-two inventory icon.
Combined bitmap colours for the corresponding top-right cell.
Combined bitmap colours for the lower-left cell of the icon.
Combined bitmap colours for the lower-right cell. The subsequent four-byte group repeats this matrix layout for the next icon.
Colour RAM nibble for the top-left icon cell, written by $69E4.
Colour RAM nibble for the icon's upper-right cell, written by $69EA.
Colour RAM nibble for the icon's lower-left cell, written by $69F0.
Colour RAM nibble for the final icon cell. The second icon's colour group follows.
Count decremented on the death path unless the title keyboard signature flag is active.
Paints twelve horizontal meter segments, each using five consecutive bitmap scanlines within one eight-byte cell, and sets the update count to twelve.
Number of energy cells still lit. A decrement selects the next emptied gauge cell and zero passes into the death path.
If the meter update count is nonzero, decrements it and rewrites five scanlines in one horizontal segment. Calls the damage handler when the count reaches zero.
When the damage cooldown permits, sets the death countdown to $80 and the cooldown to $FF. A watch at $6AC5 caught the decrement of remaining lives with the title signature flag clear.
X coordinate patched before the main impact animation slot is copied.
Y field of the impact animation's object template. The launch routine fills this byte with the source object's screen Y.
X coordinate of the secondary effect, supplied by an object or grid-coordinate launch path.
Y field of the secondary effects template, initialized before the object slot copy.
Decrements the slot's frame timer and reloads it from the configured period when it expires. Advances the shape pointer and frees the slot at shape $59.
Retrieves the slot index saved in $108D, increments $09ED, and patches the effect initializer at $6ACC with the slot coordinates before replacing the slot.
Copies the source slot's position to the effect initializer and falls through to the slot allocation path.
Saves the source X index, tests the four-effect limit and searches for a free slot. On success increments the effect counter and copies the initializer at $6ACC.
Saved X operand restored after trying to allocate an impact animation.
Calculates a cell's screen coordinates with $7F9D, patches the X field into the secondary effect template and goes to the common Y-field setup.
Copies the active object's X and Y into $6AD8, looks for a free room slot and installs the secondary impact template if space remains.
Saved X operand restored after copying the secondary effect template.
Counts down the lifetime and an emission delay. Reinitializes the delay and creates another impact with randomized offsets from the emitter whenever the interval expires.
Resolves the current room interaction, removes the entry and its visible tile, sets the rifle stock to $63 and chooses the rifle before redrawing the equipment indicator.
The handler at $76B1 increments this count while fire is down and stops incrementing at 31.
Checks current and prior active-low fire latches, then patches a jump from a handler pointer in the selected item record.
Low address byte patched into the equipment action dispatch jump.
High address byte patched into the equipment action dispatch jump.
Leading sprite shape value in the rifle projectile template.
Horizontal position of the rifle projectile, patched when a shot is allocated.
Y position in the rifle projectile initializer. The next byte is the callback type selector.
Type byte of the rifle projectile template, chosen using the release threshold. The following bytes provide its default per-slot parameters.
Signed X increment within the rifle projectile template used by the projectile movement handler.

Advances the projectile by its signed X velocity and removes it if X reaches $B4. At a direction-specific boundary within each tile, tests the terrain and converts the slot to an impact animation on a nonzero result. A clear trajectory goes through $2B26 to the next slot.
Type $10 initializer passed to the slot copier by $703C. The caller fills four coordinate bytes at $6C7D through $6C80.
Low byte of the starting fixed-point X patched into the first chaser's template.
High byte of the starting X in the first chaser's template.
Low starting Y byte patched by the first chaser's installer.
High starting Y byte in the first template, followed by the template's remaining callback parameters.
The alternate type $10 initializer selected by $6FF7. The four coordinate bytes at $6C8E through $6C91 hold the scaled room coordinates.
Low byte of the starting fixed-point X patched into the second chaser's template.
High byte paired with $6C8E in the alternate chase template.
Low starting Y byte patched by the alternate chaser's installer.
High starting Y byte in the second template, followed by the remainder of its callback state.

Advances the animation counter and, every eight updates, compares each room coordinate with the target at $0CB2. Changes the signed velocities toward that target within two units of zero and applies movement and directional terrain probes.

Subtracts the camera origin from both room coordinates. If both differences fit without a nonzero high byte, marks the slot in view, selects an animation frame and runs the drawing path with a chance of spawning a projectile.
Step magnitudes indexed by the signed velocity and the low bit of $39. The X and Y movement paths use offset bases in this table.
Remaining step magnitudes in the chase movement table. Its two velocity lookups use different starting offsets and combine adjacent entries with the animation phase.

Probes the room grid at $A600 for solid terrain on the leading Y edge, testing the next column if the entity crosses into it. On collision adjusts room Y to the next 32-unit boundary and zeros Y velocity.
Saved slot index patched into LDX during the upward terrain probe. A solid bit causes the path to align the object's room Y to the next row boundary and set its Y velocity to zero.
Probes solid terrain using Y plus $15 and the entity's room X. On collision sets the low five bits of room Y to ten and zeros Y velocity.
Saved slot index restored before testing the downwards collision bit. On a hit the path aligns Y within the current tile and clears Y velocity.
Tests bit zero in the tile attribute on the leading X edge. Also probes the tile one row below when the entity extends far enough into it. On collision adjusts room X and clears X velocity.
Saved slot index restored before testing the leftward collision bit. On a hit the path advances the edge-aligned X coordinate and zeroes X velocity.
Selects a room tile from the slot X plus $0C and current Y. On collision sets the low nibble of X to three and stops horizontal movement.
Saved slot index restored before testing the rightward collision bit. On a hit the path sets the low X nibble to three and zeroes X velocity.
Indexed animation entries read at $6D9B–$6DA7. The update reads a next index, the sprite value and a draw selector at consecutive offsets.
Second byte of each animation entry, supplying the frame's shape pointer.
Third byte of the indexed chase animation records. The chase draw path combines it with the facing flag before choosing a sprite display entry.
Reduces the slot's hit counter by the current hit strength when its in-view flag is set. On borrow clears the slot, runs the award and sound calls and turns it into an effect.
Calls the damage request at $09D0 when the slot's in-view flag is set.
Scales the spawn coordinates, copies them into the second initializer, marks the spawn record $FE, then installs the entity.
Scales $02 and $03 into two 16-bit room coordinates. X is multiplied by 16 in $02/$06, and Y by 32 in $03/$07.
Scales the spawn coordinates and writes them to the initializer at $6C73. Marks the source spawn record $FE before installing the entity.
Chooses horizontal velocity $03 or $FD by comparing the current object's X with the player's. Copies the object's launch coordinates into the projectile template before allocating a slot.
Limits the active count to three. Looks for a vacant room slot, copies the projectile template and queues the start sound when a slot is available.
Saved Y operand for the timed projectile allocation path. Restores the incoming record index after attempting a launch.
Saved X operand for the timed projectile allocation path. Restores the incoming object index after attempting a launch.
Caps the number of active timed projectiles and is decremented on their hit or expiry.
Horizontal launch position derived from the object firing the timed projectile.
Vertical launch position. The remaining initializer bytes supply the callback type, hit parameters and velocity.
Signed launch speed selected from the relative X of the player and the firing object.
Queues a sound, requests a gauge decrement, frees the projectile and decrements the active count before asking for an impact effect.
Clears the indexed entity's Y byte, decrements $70A1, requests the effect at $8FC9, and transfers control to $6B08.
Adds the slot velocity to its X coordinate and tests the next terrain cell. On contact plays the impact path and leaves the active list. A clear trajectory is queued for drawing.

Decrements the timer in the indexed interaction record. At zero, reloads the base delay with a random addition and resolves or reuses its room-tile pointer. If that tile is zero, writes $FF to the timer instead of spawning.
Patched immediate Y value used by the timer-disable path. When the resolved room tile is zero, it marks the corresponding interaction timer $FF.
Converts the interaction's cell coordinates to screen coordinates relative to the camera and patches two slot templates. A nonzero flag selects an additional call before entering $707D.
Initializer whose screen coordinates and animation pointer are filled in by $7192 before the slot copy.
Horizontal screen coordinate patched by the vertical entity initializer.
Y position in the vertical entity template, replaced before the next slot copy.
Low byte of the animation source pointer in the object's template.
High byte of the animation sequence pointer for the vertical entity. The selected record also supplies its low byte at $718B.
Stores the prepared screen coordinates and two-byte pointer in the initializer at $7183, sets spawn field two to $FE, and copies the initializer into the selected slot.

When bit zero of $39 is clear, reads the next frame through the slot's animation pointer and wraps on $FF. Adds the vertical velocity and reverses it if the terrain probe reports a nonzero attribute. Within bounds, may spawn a projectile before drawing.
Finds a room spawn entry whose marker byte has bit seven set, writes the slot's saved coordinates into it, sets type $22, and removes the active slot.
Subtracts hit strength from the slot's counter and spawns the effect. On borrow, also clears the active byte and runs the award and sound calls.
Tail call to $09D0, which gates requests on the damage counter at $09DE.
Applies hit strength to the slot counter. On borrow clears the slot and calls the award paths. Ends with the effect setup at $6B08.
Calls $9021 and calls the damage gauge routine at $6A84 eight times.
Eighteen-byte slot template based on shape value $59. $73CB copies two coordinate pairs into the template before marking the spawn record $FE and installing the slot.
First position field patched by the room spawn installer for the template beginning at $72A1.
Second position field in the same template, immediately before its object type byte.
First of the saved source coordinate pair copied from $02/$03 by $73D5.
Second saved source coordinate field in the first variant; the remaining bytes give its initial effect parameters.
Retained record with the same coordinate slots and shape value as its neighbours. Its type byte is $16 and its initializer holds different parameter and delay bytes.
Screen X in the middle template. Updated by the object spawn variant at $73AB.
Screen Y field patched at $73B2 before the middle template is copied.
Grid X field of the middle initializer's original position pair.
Grid Y field of the middle initializer. Its following fields retain the middle variant's initial directions and delay.
Eighteen-byte shape $59 template selected by $73EB. The four patched bytes at $72C6, $72C7, $72CD and $72CE hold its two coordinate pairs.
Screen position byte patched by the third spawn installer.
Vertical position byte paired with the screen X in the last template.
First of the original grid coordinates saved in the final spawn initializer.
Second byte of the second coordinate pair in the final 18-byte spawn template, patched by the handler at $73EB.

Updates the indexed entity's pause counter, vertical velocity and horizontal direction. While moving it can call $705F on its timer match. Outside the display margins, it checks the camera bounds and can return the object to the room spawn list.
Updates the corresponding coordinate fields in the selected object template and initializes the slot from the room spawn record.
Copies two coordinate pairs to the first $72A1 template, marks the room record $FE and passes the template to the common slot copier.
Transfers the spawn record's position fields to $72C5, marks the record $FE and uses the common slot copier.
Looks up the interaction in range, marks it $FE and replaces the working spawn list's terminator with the four argument bytes as a new spawn record.
Advances X in increments of four until it finds the list terminator. Copies the supplied interaction's argument tuple and terminates the list at the next slot.
A second consecutive return at the end of the interaction-to-spawn handler, before the next callable code.
Finds the current interaction and removes it and its tile. Increments the quantity at $7C17, selects equipment slot three and starts the panel and sound update.
Return following the normal return from pickup handling. It precedes the paired-tile toggle routine.

Checks the select transition and resolves the interaction record. Alternates the linked tile state stored at $A792 and $A7D2, then uses the interaction counter to choose a tile from $A93B and refreshes the room drawing.
Waits for select and a matching interaction cell, then latches the equipment action. Requests the indicator effect when $766B is below its terminal value.
Sets fuel to 80 decimal and initializes the fuel display and the 32-tick consumption interval.
When up is held and refuelling is inactive, decrements the interval. At the end of each interval it redraws the gauge and consumes one fuel unit, or calls the damage handler if fuel is already zero.
Advances the bitmap gauge animation during consumption or refuelling. The refill branch increments the fuel byte and checks for 99 decimal.
Shifts two four-byte bitmap strips through neighbouring positions, preserving the original first byte on the stack for the end of the strip.
Reverses a short panel strip transfer, moving adjacent pixel rows back and restoring the saved byte at the end.
Set from the current display threshold, controlling which halves of the fuel-depletion gauge strip are shifted.
Fuel quantity displayed in decimal. The game initializes it to $50 and decrements it in the active thrust timer path.
Countdown for consumption animation. The animator tests alignment modulo four before changing its bitmap strips.
Countdown between fuel units. The consumption path reloads it with $20.
Eight-step phase counter for one unit of animated fuel refill.
Set by a matching interaction and cleared after the refill update sequence.
Saved result of the unit-to-digit calculation, checked when choosing which portions of the refill strip to move.
Multiplies the supplied row by 64, adds the column and adds $A600 to produce the 16-bit expanded map address in $04/$05.
Checks the quantities for rifle and both bomb items. If any remain, clears the charge display, restarts equipment selection and goes to the selected weapon dispatch.
Final return byte following the alternate weapon reselection path, before the rifle action at $76B1.
While fire is held, builds the charge counter and updates the indicator. On release, uses thresholds of ten and twenty to choose the firing path.
Indexes masks by the low bits of the charge count and writes the masked pattern to the panel bitmap.
Four masks, indexed by the charge remainder modulo four, that clip the four gauge art bytes to the correct fill level.
Four bitmap pattern bytes ANDed with the partial-fill mask before writing the current charge cell.
Tests the charge counter and returns if already zero. The active path clears the counter and four bitmap rows in each of eight charge cells.
Clears the charge byte and the four pixel columns of the on-screen charge indicator.
Low destination address patched for the colour RAM write in the equipment transition.
Patched high byte of the colour RAM store for the current palette transition slot. The following lookup installs the two screen-matrix nibbles.
Low nibble and fixed high bits of the palette value are combined with this patched high-nibble immediate before the screen matrix store.
Low address patched into the equipment transition's screen matrix store.
Patched high byte of the final matrix-colour store for this transition slot. The loop then advances to the next slot.
Sixteen high nibbles unpacked from the equipment panel colour bytes at $7CF6. The equipment transition installs four consecutive entries per panel segment.
Sixteen low nibbles unpacked from the same colour bytes as $77DA. The screen update combines the high and low nibbles.
Sixteen colour RAM values from the odd bytes of the paired colour data after each 32-byte panel bitmap segment.

The equipment transition at $7CB0 indexes from the selected base at $7BCA/$7BD1. Each segment advances the source by forty bytes, copying 32 bitmap bytes and unpacking four screen and colour RAM byte pairs.
Source selected by equipment index one. Its four segments advance in forty-byte steps and use the same format as the first segment at $780A.
Panel transition data selected by equipment index two. The first 32 bytes of each segment are bitmap rows at $7CDC.
Panel transition data selected by equipment index three. The eight bytes after each bitmap segment supply four screen and colour RAM pairs at $7CEF.
Panel transition source selected by equipment index four. The segment colour fields feed the three staging arrays at $77DA, $77EA and $77FA.
Panel transition source selected by equipment index five. The later source segments can overlap the data selected by subsequent entries.
Panel transition source selected by equipment index six. Each segment supplies consecutive bitmap rows followed by the screen and colour RAM values.
Seven low address bytes for the panel transition source, selected by the equipment index.
The corresponding seven high address bytes. The transition copy propagates the carry from adding the segment offset to the low byte.
Four low address bytes for where the bitmap segments are drawn, indexed by the panel segment number.
The matching high address bytes select the four destinations beginning at $F690, $F7D0, $F910 and $FA50.
Countdown that selects the colour-map update, icon redraw and bitmap segment operations for equipment.
Equipment record index. Selection advances through seven records.
Number of the next 32-byte equipment bitmap segment to update. Initialized at the start of the panel transition.
Low byte of each indexed equipment definition's action address.
High byte patched into the equipment action dispatch from the same definition record.
Six glyph indices within each equipment record. The draw routine at $7D1C sends them individually to the bitmap text renderer.
Rifle stock byte initialized to $5A. The successful projectile allocation path decrements it at $7729.
Quantity byte of the second equipment record, decremented on successful launch by $629F.
Quantity byte of the third equipment record, decremented by the screen-effect launch path.
Mutable count addressed by the pickup handler at $744C. The reset code at $09FA clears it.
The name field updated by the room destination code. Reset restores the six default glyphs.
